issues.where: Results tables (ParT fp32, ParT AMP, ParticleNet): Paper column 'k in ...' and the Status labels 'pass, same k' / 'pass, k inside range'; the sentence 'In 5 of the 9, our k is one that gives exactly the published integer'; 'For ParticleNet, all 11 numbers ... match'
issues.problem: claims.json (sha256 9d2c955c... still matches claims.sha256) pre-registers each Rej 'exact' criterion as one specific k: ParT Hgg 16260, Wqq 3683, Zqq 4975; ParticleNet Hgg 19231, H4q 2096, Wqq 5764, Zqq 7067. The report swaps in a range of k worked out afterwards (runs/exact_match.py) and counts exact matches with it. Under the pre-registered rule the counts are: ParT fp32 2 of 9 (Hbb 188, Hcc 482; Hgg 16203, Wqq 3684, Zqq 4972 miss), ParT AMP 2 of 9 (Hbb, Tbqq), ParticleNet 5 of 9 (Hgg 19267, H4q 2097, Wqq 5761, Zqq 7071 miss). The report gives 5, 4 and 9. The range reading is arguably the better one, but it is a post-hoc redefinition and the tables present it as the pre-registered result. It is disclosed only further down, under 'Alternative readings'. Pass/fail status is unaffected, since it uses the Poisson band, which was applied correctly.
issues.fix: In each table, show the pre-registered exact result (k == the claims.json k) as its own column and state the counts 2/9, 2/9 and 5/9. Move the range-based count (5/9, 4/9, 9/9) into a column or sentence labelled 'post-hoc: any k that rounds to the published integer'. Add one sentence explaining why the single pre-registered k was a bad choice for Rej below about 550.

issues.where: Notes for the authors, first paragraph and suggestion 2
issues.problem: The text addressed to the authors says '5 of 9 ParT rejections exactly' and 'Every number in the ParticleNet row matches exactly'. Both rely on the post-hoc range criterion and not the pre-registered one. It also says the other 4 'are within 1–4 QCD jets, which is the size of AMP rounding noise'. That is not established: the AMP run, which is the authors' own setting, also misses 5 of 9 k values (by 1–5 jets), so the residual is unexplained, and fp32-vs-AMP drift only shows that drift of this size is plausible. 'Our results show they are the ones behind Table 1' is also stronger than the evidence, since 4 ParT counts differ.
issues.fix: Say 'match at the printed precision' (true for all 11 ParticleNet and 7 of 9 ParT numbers... more precisely, every Rej rounds to the published integer in 5 of 9 ParT and 9 of 9 ParticleNet cases) and avoid 'exactly'. Replace 'which is the size of AMP rounding noise' with 'comparable to the 1–7 jet differences between our own fp32 and AMP runs; we cannot pin down the cause (GPU, torch/cuDNN version or old weaver)'. Change 'show' to 'strongly indicate'.

issues.where: Alternative readings, last bullet: 'Both are off by 1–5 jets ... (our fp32 and AMP runs differ from each other by the same amount)'
issues.problem: From score.json, fp32 and AMP k differ by 1 (Hcc, H4q, Hqql, Tbqq), 2 (Tbl), 3 (Zqq), 6 (Wqq: 3684 vs 3690) and 7 (Hgg: 16203 vs 16210). That is up to 7 jets, not 'the same amount' as 1–5.
issues.fix: Write 'our fp32 and AMP runs differ from each other by 0–7 jets' and give the per-column differences.

issues.where: What it took, item 4: 'Speed was about 3,000 jets/s for ParT and 2,500 jets/s for ParticleNet'
issues.problem: The wall times in run_all.log give: ParT fp32 15:26:15–17:40:57 (8,082 s) ≈ 2,470 jets/s; ParT AMP 17:40:57–19:28:55 (6,478 s) ≈ 3,090 jets/s; ParticleNet 19:28:55–22:05:47 (9,412 s) ≈ 2,125 jets/s. The ParticleNet figure is about 18% too high, and fp32 ParT ran nearer 2,500 than 3,000. This also contradicts 'No number in this report was estimated or typed by hand'.
issues.fix: State the rates from the logs (≈2,470 fp32 ParT with the variant interleaved under the lock, ≈3,090 AMP ParT, ≈2,125 ParticleNet), or drop the rates. Either way, keep only numbers that a file produces.

issues.where: What it took, item 2: 'Size: 30,370,816,000 B, equal to the server's Content-Length'
issues.problem: runs/download.sh compares the file size with a hard-coded 30370816000 taken from the triage notes (Zenodo listing). Neither download.log nor any other file in the folder records a Content-Length header from this run.
issues.fix: Write 'equal to the size listed by Zenodo (30,370,816,000 B, recorded in triage)', or capture a HEAD/Content-Length now and keep it in a log file.

issues.where: Notes for the authors, suggestion 1: 'We checked that the data loader is not the cause. Inputs are identical on all real particles'
issues.problem: The loader comparison in runs/diag_weaver053/diag.log covers only the first 512 H→bb jets of one file (HToBB_100.root), on CPU. The sentence to the authors generalises it to all inputs. The diagnosis section is also silent that padded slots differ (max |diff| 824 in pf_vectors), which points to a change in padding as well.
issues.fix: Say 'on the first 512 H→bb jets of HToBB_100.root the 0.5.3 loader gives the same values as 0.4.17 on every real particle (padded slots differ but are masked), and the 0.4.17 model scores are unchanged on 0.5.3 inputs'.

issues.where: Notes for the authors, suggestion 1: '0.5.3 (on PyPI since 2026-06-22)'
issues.problem: The only evidence in the folder is the v0.5.3 git tag date (comment in env/setup_variant_0.5.3.sh). No PyPI upload date was checked.
issues.fix: Write 'tagged 2026-06-22', or check the PyPI upload time and cite it.

issues.where: What it took: 'The command differs from train_JetClass.sh only in how it is run'
issues.problem: For the ParT main run this is not true. train_JetClass.sh passes --use-amp for ParT, and the main fp32 run drops it. That was pre-registered (D9), but the sentence lists only --predict, the training args, per-group calls and --num-workers.
issues.fix: Add to the list: 'ParT main run without --use-amp (fp32, pre-registered D9); the AMP variant keeps it'.

issues.problem: 0.86050855 is only 8.6e-6 (171 jets) above the 0.8605 rounding edge, and 0.0005 below the paper value. The status follows the pre-registered rule, but a reader cannot tell how close it sits to the edge.
issues.fix: Add a short note: 'rounds to 0.861 by 171 jets; diff −0.00049 is half the pre-registered ±0.001 band'.

issues.problem: The DOI given is the arXiv DOI, not a DOI of the PMLR paper. Nothing in the working folder records the 64 GB total RAM; the triage notes and the task only state 31 GB available to WSL.
issues.fix: Label it 'arXiv DOI' (PMLR has none). Either drop '64 GB' or source it with a logged command (e.g. systeminfo or wmic output saved in runs/).

issues.problem: The report never says that Table 1 was produced with the older hqucms/weaver and not weaver-core, a known source of residual differences recorded in claims.json D10. This matters for reading the 1–5 jet residuals and the 0.5.3 result.
issues.fix: Add one line to 'Alternative readings' or 'What it took': 'Table 1 predates weaver-core (repo switched on 2022-12-15, commit 29ef32b5); 0.4.17 is the closest released version, not the code that made the table'.

issues.problem: 'reviewed by a human before publication' and 'a human approved publication' describe a step that has not happened at this stage. 'This was a single-agent run' also contradicts the same paragraph, which describes separate pre-registration, reviewer and reviser agents.
issues.fix: Keep the human-approval sentence only once it is true (or mark it pending). Rephrase to 'a single agent did the computation; there was no blind recomputation by a second agent'.
